title: Map Area Calculator: Measure Any Shape
description: Measure the area of any shape drawn on the map with the Map Area Calculator — geodesic polygon area in acres, hectares, square miles and more. Free.
summary_sentence: For example, a rectangle drawn between four map coordinates can measure 6.08 km² — 1,501 acres — computed on the curved Earth, not on the flat fiction of the screen.
quick_answer: The Map Area Calculator measures the surface area of a polygon you draw on the map, computed geodesically on the Earth's sphere. Drop the corners of a field, lake or parcel and read the area in acres, hectares or square miles — accurate from garden to county.

body.t: Four corners spanning about 3.75 km by 1.6 km measure 6.08 km² (1,501 acres, 2.35 sq mi) on the sphere. The same rectangle computed flat would read slightly differently at its latitude — the geodesic method is why the number travels between tools unchanged.

faq: By spherical polygon geometry (the Chamberlain–Duquette method family): the boundary's great-circle edges enclose a surface area on the reference sphere, converted to your chosen unit. It is the standard approach of serious web-mapping libraries.
How accurate is a drawn measurement?

The geometry is exact; the drawing is human. Zoom in, place corners on the true boundary, and expect agreement with surveyed areas within a percent or two — good for planning, never a substitute for the survey itself.
Can I measure several separate areas?
Draw each polygon in turn and add the results — or draw one boundary around a study region when the total footprint is the question. The tool prices the shape you close.
For a shape with a hole (a building's courtyard, a lake's island), measure the outer polygon and subtract the hole's own measurement. Two honest numbers beat one complicated one.
Does terrain slope inflate the area?
Map area is plan (horizontal) area — the deed convention. A steep hillside's true surface is larger; specialised surface-area tools address that different question.

None in the result: geodesic area is computed on the sphere, so a square kilometre near the pole measures the same ground as one at the equator — unlike pixel-counting on a Mercator screen, which would lie by the cosine.
Self-intersecting polygons (a figure-eight) have no single honest area — the tool expects a simple boundary. Split bowties into two honest polygons.
Units for a farm versus a forest?
Acres in the US, hectares almost everywhere else; the calculator reports both because land, like weather, ignores the reader's habits.
